references.text: Aaron shall make atonement on the horns of the altar once a year with the blood of the sin offering for atonement. This illustrates the annual atonement ritual performed on the altar.
Describes the sin offering involving a bull, including the blood ritual and the atonement made to cleanse from sin.
Moses slaughtered the bull, took its blood, and applied it to the horns of the altar all around with his finger, cleansing the altar from sin. This parallels the consecration of the altar.
The Day of Atonement where the high priest makes atonement on the altar with blood to cleanse it from Israel's impurities.
Ezekiel describes the cleansing of the altar with blood from a sin-offering bull over seven days, paralleling the consecration of the altar.
Describes the cleansing of the sanctuary with blood from a young bull as a sin offering, applied to the doorposts and the corners of the altar.

The book of Hebrews explains that almost everything is cleansed with blood under the law, and that heavenly things must be purified with better sacrifices. This connects Old Testament atonement to Christ's perfect sacrifice.
Blood from bulls and goats cannot take away sins. This shows the limitation of Old Testament sin offerings fulfilled by Christ.
Ezekiel 43:22 refers directly to the consecration ritual in Exodus, using the bull as a reference point for cleansing.
Ezekiel 43:20 details the practical procedure (blood on the horns) for the atonement of the altar commanded in Exodus 29:36.
Leviticus 16:18 shows the execution of atonement for the altar with bull blood as required in Exodus 29:36.
Ezekiel 43:25 confirms and expands on the requirement for a daily sin offering for the cleansing of the altar from Exodus 29:36.
Exodus 40:10 describes the actual performance of anointing and consecration as commanded in Exodus 29:36.
